newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank mulls reserve requirement change.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank mulls reserve requirement change.

text.p: The Czech National Bank said on Thursday it was considering a change in its new formula to calculate minimum reserve requirements for mortgage banks issuing state-supported mortgage bonds.

CNB spokesman Martin Svehla said the CNB was negotiating with mortgage banks "with the aim of eliminating the impact of changes in methodolgy of the creation of minimum reserves on interest rates from state-supported mortgage loans."
A central bank measure which takes effect on September 26 will include all revenue from the issuance of securities on the calculation of 11.5 percent in minimum reserve requirements.
"The intention is to exclude (from assets against which minimum reserves are calculated) the part which is used to re-finance mortgage credits," Svehla told Reuters.
He said this would help to keep interest rates on mortgages which have state subsidies at current levels.
There was no indication on when the change might be agreed.

To encourage new housing construction, the government this year launched a programme whereby it would grant subsidies for reductions by up to four percentage points on interest rates for housing mortgages on qualified projects.

But the central bank has been also trying to tighten the money supply to slow domestic. It raised minimum reserve requirements against standard deposits to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent from the beginning of August.
